messages:
Maya K.: quick share — ran an empirical split-bench for speculative decoding on the new 7B-q4 build. saw nice latency wins but one odd long-form regression. posting short notes + command so we can triage.

Ravi P.: nice, do you mean spec decoding where smaller model proposes tokens and large model verifies?

Maya K.: yup — small proposer (3.5B-ish) + main model (7B-q4) verifier. budget=12 tokens, greedy proposer, synchronous verify.

Samir: rough numbers? p50/p95, token/sec, any quality metrics?

Maya K.: short summary: p50 latency ~1.7x speedup, p95 ~1.5x. tokens/sec increases ~65% on avg. automated QA/EM-style metrics show delta within noise for short Q/A but rouge/faithfulness on long summarization dropped ~1.8% absolute on ROUGE-L on our 500-example news-summary set.

Priya L.: 1.8% ROUGE-L is concerning. what's sampling/temperature? could be proposer bias causing unsafe prefixes.

Maya K.: eval configs: temp=0.0 (deterministic), top_p=0.95 for proposer, verifier greedy. quantization: q4_k_mixed (our standard). run command:

```bash
python eval/run_splitbench.py \
  --model redwood/7b-q4 \
  --proposer redwood/3b-flat \
  --budget 12 \
  --proposer-top-p 0.95 \
  --temperature 0.0 \
  --dataset news-summary-500 \
  --seed 42 \
  --cache-prefix true
```

Maya K.: raw metrics from the run (500 ex):

```text
baseline (no spec): p50=210ms p95=540ms tokens/s=78 ROUGE-L=37.4
speculative (budget=12): p50=123ms p95=362ms tokens/s=128 ROUGE-L=35.6
-> latency p50 1.7x improvement, tokens/s +62%, ROUGE-L -1.8 absolute
```

EvalBot: automated eval note — sample size 500, bootstrap CI for ROUGE-L ~ ±0.9. observed delta -1.8 is ~2 sigma. recommend human spot-check.

Ravi P.: did you try with proposer temperature lower? proposer might be overconfident and push fluent but off-target tokens. also curious about cache-prefix on/off.

Maya K.: I ran two quick ablations:

```text
- budget 6: p50=150ms p95=410ms tokens/s=102 ROUGE-L=36.4 (-1.0)
- cache-prefix=false: p50=140ms p95=380ms tokens/s=110 ROUGE-L=36.0 (-1.4)
- proposer-temp=0.0 (forced) => tiny perf loss vs default, ROUGE-L ~36.1
```

Priya L.: that pattern suggests regret flips near the end of long outputs — verifier accepts proposer continuations that later cause halluc. maybe proposer beam=1 too narrow? or proposer vocabulary mismatch with quantized verifier causing scoring weirdness.

Samir: another angle: verifier's kv-cache precision (q4) might poorly rank proposer tokens vs baseline logits. we should try a run with verifier in fp16 (no quant) but same proposer to check.

Maya K.: queued a fp16 verifier run (same seed). initial quick run (50 ex) shows ROUGE-L ~36.9 (vs 37.4 baseline). latency drop still present but slightly smaller. implies quantization interacts with spec pipeline.

TriageBot: linked issue created — #ml/spec-decode-empirical-1769999999 — contains artifacts (configs, logs, samples): https://redwood.internal/issue/1234

Ravi P.: next experimental checklist I propose:
- re-run full 500 with fp16 verifier
- run human eval on 100 long-summary samples (pairwise blind: baseline vs spec)
- try proposer beam=3 and budget sweep [6,12,18]
- log verifier acceptance rates, token-level edit distance vs baseline

Maya K.: agreed. I'll kick off fp16 500 run overnight, add beam=3 sweep, and export the 100 examples for human eval in the triage issue.

Priya L.: small note — annotate where proposer introduced earlier entity hallucination (we saw 7 cases). That will help root cause.

Maya K.: will do. if fp16 closes >0.7 of the gap, we might prioritize a quantized-rerank fallback (run spec path but fallback to non-spec for long docs).

Samir: also capture memory / GPU-util numbers — speculative adds proposer overhead but can change memory pressure and scheduling.

Maya K.: adding perf traces + pprof. thanks everyone. will post a follow-up with the full fp16 numbers tomorrow. :thumbsup:
